review.headline: Drew got caught as the Sphinx twice, and the Farm swept a lopsided game.
review.summary: Drew was the Meowfia Sphinx in both rounds, and his false claims were broken within a few messages both times. In round 1, Ellis's Turkey disproved his Tit story. In round 2, Casey, the real Owl, and Alex's Kookaburra both caught him at once. Finley, his unknown teammate, never came under suspicion, but he also never helped, and he left his Wink unused. Casey won 61 to Drew's 5. Two phantom cards from a confused report helped her.

rounds.recap: Drew, the Sphinx, claimed Tit and said he visited Ellis. Ellis revealed he was the Turkey: any visitor would have gained an egg, and Drew's nest was still 5. Drew changed his story to visiting Finley, which looked worse. The table called CAW quickly and 17 of 18 thrown cards hit Drew. He was Meowfia.

Alex's Kookaburra had no visitors, so its result was reliable, and it named Drew as the Sphinx. Drew counterclaimed Owl, but Casey was the real Owl and had seen a Sphinx and a Mouser visit Ellis. The day ended after five messages, and everyone except the two cats threw at Drew.

highlights.text: Ellis used the Turkey's passive egg-laying to prove that Drew's visit never happened. Nest sizes worked as evidence, which is clean and satisfying.
Finley, the Floofer, pushed hard on Drew without knowing they were teammates, and that helped sink his own side.
Drew claimed Owl in front of the real Owl, and Casey's report confirmed Alex's unconfused Kookaburra read. The two pieces of evidence locked together.
Finley threw a single card at Casey just for the consolation return. It was smart damage control from a losing Meowfia.

confusions.what: Said 'Third time: Kookaburra' in her first message of the day. She had never claimed before. She also said Alex's Falcon visit 'confirmed' her role, but a Falcon only learns who its target visited.
Was the real Tit and knew Drew's Tit claim was false (her survey cites it), but never said so. She spoke only to call CAW.
Said Alex 'lost 2 eggs'. Alex's nest was 3 because he threw 4 cards in round 1 and drew 2 at setup. No eggs were stolen.
His Hawk visited Casey and gained no egg, which proves Casey is Farm. He still rated her 40% Meowfia, his second-highest suspicion.

Her Falcon saw Finley visit Ellis. Casey saw only a Mouser and a Sphinx visit Ellis, and Drew was the claimed Sphinx, so Finley had to be the Mouser. Blair never connected this and rated Finley only 30%.
As the Sphinx, he named Falcon after reasoning about Kookaburra or Turkey. That choice left him blind to the Turkey, which was the role that then exposed his lie.

design_notes: Confused players really draw cards for phantom eggs. Casey got S10 and S12 (22 points) from a false report and banked them. Decide whether confusion should cost or pay real cards. Right now it is a windfall. The log line 'hugged: no effect at tier 50' is also unclear. Casey's report never said she was hugged or that she learned no role.

Information roles stack up and leave the Meowfia nothing to hide behind. With Turkey, Owl, Kookaburra and Falcon all available, any claim that names a visit gets checked. Each day ended within 7 messages via CAW, and both votes were near-unanimous. Tension was low.

The Mouser's Wink never mattered. Finley said nothing in round 2 and the day closed before a Wink felt useful. A Wink on Alex or Casey before they spoke could have changed the round. With three CAW calls able to end the day so fast, the Wink has no window to be used.

The Sphinx is a liability. Its forced visit to a known role puts it in the visitor lists of Owls and Eagles. It also gives no egg changes to hide behind, so the Sphinx must invent a claim that someone holding the role can contradict. Drew was the Sphinx both rounds and lost both, with 5 points in total.

Meowfia never won, so the two cat players ended with 4–5 points and the Farm players with 38–61. Over 2 rounds, a player who rolls Meowfia twice has no route back. Consider more rounds, or a better consolation for the losing side.
review.title: Sphinx Caught Twice
